evals.prompt: Update evals/files/project/pr-body.md for the top layer of a two-layer stack. The project declares no issue tracker, description template, or contributing guide. Work only on this layer: it caps idempotent HTTP retries at three attempts; the lower layer's retry telemetry is context, not part of this change. The current draft contains an old `## Human and Agent Roles` section copied from another layer. Use the supplied change summary and AI notes, produce the complete final description, write it back, validate it, and report the result.
evals.expected_output: The updated body uses the default four-section structure, states that no issue tracker applies rather than silently omitting the tracker exception, removes the old Human and Agent Roles section, carries exactly one valid AI Usage section for the retry cap only, leaves the unhandled review row at n/a with an empty decision-record cell and puts the no-comments statement after the table, and does not add tracker labels, Project fields, or dates.
assertions: The body uses the default Motivation, Changes, Testing, and AI Usage sections.
The old Human and Agent Roles section is removed rather than retained beside AI Usage.
Exactly one AI Usage section and one AI-DECLARATION block remain.
The AI Usage table records this retry-cap layer only and does not repeat the lower layer's telemetry work.
The AI-DECLARATION version is 0.1.2 and its badge equals the highest row level.
The body reports the supplied passing test evidence without claiming an unrun check.
The review row remains n/a with an empty decision-record cell, and the no-comments statement follows the table.
Motivation states that no issue tracker applies instead of silently omitting the tracker exception.
The update does not invent tracker labels, Project fields, or dates.

evals.prompt: Prepare the `Changes` section for the change in evals/files/workspace-dependencies by comparing the base manifests under base/ with the current package manifests. The project uses the default description structure. Report affected package responsibilities and every added or removed runtime dependency edge, including any reverse edge, without inventing a dependency that the manifests do not contain.
evals.expected_output: The section derives edges from the base-to-head manifest diff, names the app and core responsibilities, records the added app → core edge and the removed app → legacy edge, preserves the existing core → app reverse edge, and does not claim that the reverse edge is absent.
assertions: The section states the app and core package responsibilities.
The dependency edges are derived from the base-to-head manifest diff.
The added runtime edge is written as app → core.
The removed runtime edge is written as app → legacy.
The existing core → app runtime edge is reported rather than called absent.
The section does not hide the dependency cycle behind a composition-only explanation.

evals.prompt: Update evals/files/tracked-issues/motivation.md using the declared tracker and its recorded issue state. This change resolves Issue #17 and takes context from Issue #18; both same-project issues must be visible in Motivation. Issue #19 and change request #20 do not track it. The supplied non-counting-reference fixture contains hidden, code-fenced, inline-code, and cross-project forms that do not count as visible same-project references. Write the Motivation section back and report what you changed.

The references are outside HTML comments, code fences, and inline code. Issue #19, change request #20, and cross-project issue references are not presented as tracked issue references.
assertions: Motivation states the problem in one sentence.
Visible same-project references to both Issue #17 and Issue #18 are present.
Issue #17 uses a resolving keyword and Issue #18 uses an informational keyword.
The qualifying references are outside HTML comments, code fences, and inline code.
Hidden, code-fenced, inline-code, and cross-project references are not counted as tracked issue references.
Issue #19 and change request #20 are not presented as tracked issue references.
